messages.subject: error when using inla.rgeneric.define()
parts:
Hi all,

I am a new user of INLA, and I am trying to build a new latent model for a spatial-varying coefficients model. For simplicity, I assume that the intercept beta(s) ~ MVN(mu0, Q^{-1}),
where Q = prec * exp(D/rho), with D being the distance matrix. 

Here is my code for generating a new latent model:

'inla.rgeneric.beta.model' <- function(
    cmd = c("graph", "Q", "mu", "initial", "log.norm.const", "log.prior", "quit"),
    theta = NULL) {
  envir = parent.env(environment())
  interpret.theta <- function() {
    return(list(prec = exp(theta[1L]),
                rho = 1/(1+exp(-theta[2L])),
                mu0 = theta[3L]))
  }
  graph <- function() {
    return (Q())
  }
  Q <- function() {
    require(Matrix)
    param <- interpret.theta()
    A <- param$prec * exp(D/param$rho)
    return(inla.as.sparse(A))
  }
  mu <- function() {
    param <- interpret.theta()
    return(param$mu0)
  }
  log.norm.const <- function() {
    param <- interpret.theta()
    n <- nrow(D)
    Q <- param$prec * exp(D/param$rho)
    res <- n * (-0.5 * log(2 * pi)) + 0.5 * Matrix::determinant(Q, logarithm = T)
    return(res)
  }
  log.prior <- function() {
    param = interpret.theta()
    # since transformation
    res <- dgamma(param$prec, 1, 1, log = T) + log(param$prec) +
      log(1) + log(param$rho) + log(1 - param$rho) +
      dnorm(param$mu0, 0, 1, log = T)
    return(res)
  }
  initial <- function() {
    return(rep(0, 0, 0))
  }
  quit <- function() {
    return(invisible())
  }
 
  if (!length(theta)) theta = initial()
  val <- do.call(match.arg(cmd), args = list())
  return(val)
}

And here is the data:
library(spgwr)
data(georgia)
Dist0 <- as.matrix(dist(data.frame(gSRDF$Latitude, gSRDF$Longitud)))
Dist01 <- Dist0 / max(Dist0)
D <- Dist01
beta.model <- inla.rgeneric.define(inla.rgeneric.beta.model, D = D)
f.beta <- PctBach ~ 1 + f(idx, model = beta.model)
m.beta <- inla(f.beta, data = data.frame(gSRDF, idx = 1:159), family = "gaussian", verbose = T)

Error occurs but I am sorry that I cannot understand what the error message means. Could you help me to figure it out?


Best,
Kurt
